subproblems.title: Mass of a represented current is at most its representing measure
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P (= Euclid P) be any set, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity representation of T in U (IMRep U n with R.Represents T, i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^n(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), H^n = μHE[n]). Then for every set W ⊆ ℝ^P, M_W(T) = T.massOn W ≤ μ_R(W). Here μ_R = R.measure = θ·H^n⌞M (its outer-measure value if W is not Borel), and M_W(T) is the supremum in [0, ∞] of ofReal T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), T.massOn W ≤ R.measure W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1, 2 and 4 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 1.1–1.7, 2.4–2.6 and Remark 3.2(3)), specialized to the upper bound. It is stated for an arbitrary set W: neither openness of U or W nor W ⊆ U is used, because the argument compares with μ_R(tsupport ω). This statement is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dor_ims_massOn_le_measure (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.imrep_mass_and_support-a1.mass_upper_bound-a1, candidate fae4fd1e831d10c18bba18fe6f9e5711d59b1ac2), reused at its byte-identical frozen type. Its accepted Lean proof makes the same comparison with μ_R(tsupport ω) by a slightly different route: it integrates against R.measure (helper dor_ims_action_eq_integral: T(ω) = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ_R with an integrable integrand) and uses the duality helper dor_ims_unitOrientation_dual. The argument below is written against H^n⌞M.
Notation. e_0, …, e_{P−1} is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P and ⟨·,·⟩ the inner product. Λ^n := Covector (Euclid P) n is the space of continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P. 𝓘 is the finite set of strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P, and e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}). |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I∈𝓘} α(e_I)²)^{1/2}. M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, ν := H^n⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M, μ := R.measure = ν.withDensity θ. Thus μ(A) = ∫⁻_A θ dν for Borel A, and for an arbitrary A, μ(A) = inf{μ(B) : B ⊇ A Borel}; in particular μ is monotone on all sets. 𝒜_W is the set of ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) = TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, and M_W(T) = T.massOn W = sup{ofReal T(ω) : ω ∈ 𝒜_W} in [0, ∞].
1. (Determinant covectors.) For I ∈ 𝓘 let dx^I(v_0, …, v_{n−1}) := det(⟨e_{I(a)}, v_b⟩)_{a,b<n}. This is a continuous alternating n-linear form: it is linear in each column, two equal arguments give two equal columns, and it is a polynomial in the coordinates.
 - For I, J ∈ 𝓘, dx^I(e_J) = det(δ_{I(a),J(b)}), which is 1 if I = J (the identity matrix).
 - If I ≠ J it is 0: strictly increasing maps with the same image coincide, so some J(b) lies outside the image of I and the b-th column vanishes.
 - For n = 0, 𝓘 = {∅} and dx^∅ = 1.
2. (Expansion.) Every α ∈ Λ^n satisfies α = Σ_{I∈𝓘} α(e_I)·dx^I.
 - By multilinearity, an n-linear form is determined by its values on all tuples e_K = (e_{K(0)}, …, e_{K(n−1)}), K : Fin n → Fin P.
 - For an alternating form, such a value is 0 when K is not injective.
 - An injective K is uniquely K = I∘σ with I ∈ 𝓘 and σ a permutation of Fin n, and then the value is sign(σ) times the value at e_I.
 - Hence two alternating n-linear forms that agree on every e_I (I ∈ 𝓘) are equal. Both sides agree on every e_J by step 1.
3. (Pointwise duality, parent step 1.) Let τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P and α ∈ Λ^n. Then |α(τ)| ≤ |α|.
 Proof:
 - Let A be the P × n matrix A_{ib} := ⟨e_i, τ_b⟩, and for I ∈ 𝓘 let A_I := (⟨e_{I(a)}, τ_b⟩)_{a,b}, so dx^I(τ) = det A_I. By step 2, α(τ) = Σ_I α(e_I)·det A_I.
 - By Parseval, (AᵀA)_{bc} = Σ_i ⟨e_i, τ_b⟩⟨e_i, τ_c⟩ = ⟨τ_b, τ_c⟩ = δ_{bc}, i.e. AᵀA = 1_n.
 - The Cauchy–Binet formula det(AᵀA) = Σ_{I∈𝓘} (det A_I)² therefore gives Σ_I (det A_I)² = det 1_n = 1.
   Proof of the formula: det(AᵀA) = Σ_σ sign(σ) ∏_b Σ_i A_{ib}A_{iσ(b)} = Σ_{K : Fin n → Fin P} (∏_b A_{K(b),b})·det(A_{K(a),c})_{a,c}. The determinant vanishes unless K is injective. For K = I∘π with I ∈ 𝓘 and π a permutation it equals sign(π)·det A_I, and Σ_π sign(π) ∏_b A_{I(π(b)),b} = det A_I.
 - By the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality in ℝ^𝓘, |α(τ)| ≤ (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2}·(Σ_I (det A_I)²)^{1/2} = |α|.
 Edge cases: for n = 0, τ is empty and α(τ) = α() with |α| = |α()|. If n > P, no orthonormal n-family exists and there is nothing to prove.
4. (Unit orientations.) If IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q, there is an orthonormal τ with ζ(α) = α(τ) for all α, or ζ(α) = −α(τ) for all α. By step 3, |ζ(α)| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ Λ^n.
5. (A.e. bound, parent step 2.) By the field R.orients, for ν-a.e. x there is Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q. By step 4, for ν-a.e. x, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α ∈ Λ^n.
6. (Reduction.) Since M_W(T) is a supremum, it suffices to show ofReal T(ω) ≤ μ(W) for every ω ∈ 𝒜_W. Fix such ω and let K := tsupport ω.
 - K is compact (ω has compact support), hence closed and Borel.
 - K ⊆ W by admissibility.
7. (Pointwise comparison.) Put f(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) ∈ ℝ. By R.Represents T, T(ω) = R.action ω = ∫ f dν, the Bochner integral over M with respect to H^n. For ν-a.e. x (those of step 5):
 - if x ∈ K, then f(x) ≤ θ(x)·|ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ θ(x)·|ω(x)| ≤ θ(x), using θ(x) ≥ 0 and |ω(x)| ≤ 1;
 - if x ∉ K, then ω(x) = 0 (x ∉ tsupport ω), so f(x) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(0) = 0.
 Hence ofReal f(x) ≤ θ(x)·1_K(x) in [0, ∞] for ν-a.e. x.
8. (Integration.) First, ofReal(∫ f dν) ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal(f) dν:
 - if f is not ν-integrable, ∫ f dν = 0 by convention and ofReal 0 = 0;
 - if it is, ∫ f dν ≤ ∫ max(f, 0) dν = toReal(∫⁻ ofReal f dν), and ofReal(toReal a) ≤ a for every a ∈ [0, ∞].
 Next, by monotonicity of the lower integral and step 7, ∫⁻ ofReal f dν ≤ ∫⁻ θ·1_K dν = ∫⁻_K θ dν = μ(K). The last equality is the definition of withDensity on the Borel set K.
 Finally, μ(K) ≤ μ(W) because K ⊆ W and μ is monotone.
9. (Conclusion.) Thus ofReal T(ω) = ofReal(∫ f dν) ≤ μ(W) for every ω ∈ 𝒜_W. Taking the supremum, T.massOn W ≤ R.measure W.
proof_key_steps: Cauchy–Binet duality: for orthonormal τ, α(τ) = Σ_I α(e_I) det A_I with Σ_I (det A_I)² = 1, so |α(τ)| ≤ |α|.
By R.orients, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for H^n⌞M-a.e. x and all α.
For admissible ω with K = tsupport ω: ofReal(θ·ξ(ω)) ≤ θ·1_K a.e. and ofReal(∫ f) ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal f, so ofReal T(ω) ≤ ∫⁻_K θ dH^n⌞M = μ_R(K) ≤ μ_R(W).
Take the supremum over admissible ω.

Then μ_R(W) ≤ M_W(T) = T.massOn W for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P (W need not lie in U). Here μ_R = R.measure = θ·H^n⌞M, and M_W(T) is the supremum in [0, ∞] of ofReal T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1, 2, 3 and 5 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 2.4–2.6 and Remark 3.2(3)), preceded by a reduction from an arbitrary open W to the open set W ∩ U ⊆ U. This statement is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dor_ims_measure_le_massOn (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.imrep_mass_and_support-a1.mass_lower_bound-a1, candidate 57cebee2fbae5e013e3b0e4191cd38bc03b89473), reused at its byte-identical frozen type. Its accepted Lean proof packages steps 8–12 differently: it applies Lusin to L∘ξ, takes V as a thickening of K', and uses one smooth admissible form from the helper dor_ims_smooth_unit_approx that is within δ of L∘ξ on K'. That needs no dominated convergence. The argument below is the parent's step 5.
Notation.
- e_0, …, e_{P−1} is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P and ⟨·,·⟩ the inner product.
- Λ^n := Covector (Euclid P) n and Λ_n := MultiVector P n = (Λ^n →L[ℝ] ℝ).
- 𝓘 is the set of strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P, e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}), and |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I∈𝓘} α(e_I)²)^{1/2}.
- M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, ν := H^n⌞M and μ := R.measure = ν.withDensity θ. So μ(A) = ∫⁻_A θ dν for Borel A, μ ≪ ν, and μ is monotone and countably subadditive.
- 𝒜_W = {ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) : tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x}, and M_W(T) = T.massOn W = sup{ofReal T(ω) : ω ∈ 𝒜_W}.
1. (Covector algebra.) For I ∈ 𝓘 put dx^I(v) := det(⟨e_{I(a)}, v_b⟩)_{a,b}. It is a continuous alternating n-linear form with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} for I, J ∈ 𝓘: strictly increasing maps with equal image coincide, so for I ≠ J some column vanishes.
 - Every α ∈ Λ^n equals Σ_{I∈𝓘} α(e_I)·dx^I. Both sides are alternating n-linear and agree on every e_J. An alternating n-linear form is determined by its values on the e_J, J ∈ 𝓘: by multilinearity it is determined by its values on all e_K, which vanish for non-injective K and equal sign(σ)·α(e_J) for K = J∘σ.
 - Consequently α ↦ (α(e_I))_{I∈𝓘} is a linear injection, and |·| is the Euclidean norm of this coefficient vector. So |·| is a norm on Λ^n: continuous, with |cα| = |c|·|α|.
2. (Duality with equality case, parent step 1.) Let τ be an orthonormal n-family. Let A be the P × n matrix (⟨e_i, τ_b⟩), and for I ∈ 𝓘 let A_I := (⟨e_{I(a)}, τ_b⟩)_{a,b}, so dx^I(τ) = det A_I and α(τ) = Σ_I α(e_I) det A_I by step 1.
 - AᵀA = (⟨τ_b, τ_c⟩)_{b,c} = 1_n.
 - The Cauchy–Binet formula gives Σ_I (det A_I)² = det(AᵀA) = 1. Proof: det(AᵀA) = Σ_σ sign σ ∏_b Σ_i A_{ib}A_{iσ(b)} = Σ_K ∏_b A_{K(b),b}·det(A_{K(a),c})_{a,c}. Only injective K = I∘π contribute, each with sign(π)·det A_I, and Σ_π sign(π) ∏_b A_{I(π(b)),b} = det A_I.
 Hence:
 (a) |α(τ)| ≤ |α| for all α, by the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality.
 (b) α_τ := Σ_I det(A_I)·dx^I has α_τ(e_J) = det A_J. So |α_τ| = (Σ_J (det A_J)²)^{1/2} = 1 and α_τ(τ) = Σ_I det(A_I)·dx^I(τ) = Σ_I (det A_I)² = 1.
 Edge cases: for n = 0, 𝓘 = {∅}, det A_∅ = 1 and α_τ = 1. If n > P there is no orthonormal n-family.
3. (The dual map.) Define L : Λ_n → Λ^n, L(ζ) := Σ_{I∈𝓘} ζ(dx^I)·dx^I, a linear (hence continuous) map between finite-dimensional spaces. If IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q, then ζ = ε·(α ↦ α(τ)) for an orthonormal τ and some ε ∈ {1, −1}. So ζ(dx^I) = ε·det A_I and L(ζ) = ε·α_τ, and by step 2:
 (i) |ζ(α)| ≤ |α| for all α;
 (ii) |L(ζ)| = 1;
 (iii) ζ(L(ζ)) = ε²·α_τ(τ) = 1.
4. (Good points and measurability, parent step 2.)
 - By R.orients, ν-a.e. x has some Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q, so (i)–(iii) hold for ζ = ξ(x) at ν-a.e. x.
 - ξ is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient), so there is a Borel map ξ₀ : ℝ^P → Λ_n with ξ = ξ₀ ν-a.e.
 - Choose a Borel ν-null set Z containing all x at which ξ(x) is not a unit orientation or ξ(x) ≠ ξ₀(x); every null set has a Borel null superset. Since μ ≪ ν, μ(Z) = 0.
 - Put β₀ := L ∘ ξ₀, a Borel map ℝ^P → Λ^n.
 For x ∉ Z: ξ(x) = ξ₀(x), |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α, |β₀(x)| = 1 and ξ(x)(β₀(x)) = 1.
5. (Radon facts, parent step 3.)
 (R1) For compact K ⊆ U, μ(K) = ∫⁻_K θ dν = ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞, by the field locallyIntegrable_mult.
 (R2) μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0: ℝ^P ∖ U is closed, hence Borel, and ν(ℝ^P ∖ U) ≤ ν(ℝ^P ∖ M) = 0 because M ⊆ U.
 (R3) (Inner approximation.) For open G ⊆ ℝ^P, let G_j := {x : |x| ≤ j, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ G) ≥ 1/(j+1)}, or the closed ball of radius j about 0 if G = ℝ^P. These sets are compact (closed and bounded), increase with j, lie in G, and have union G because G is open. By continuity from below, μ(G_j) → μ(G).
 (R4) (Outer approximation.) Let K ⊆ G with K compact, G open, G ⊆ U, and η > 0. Then there is an open V with K ⊆ V, closure V compact, closure V ⊆ G and μ(V ∖ K) < η.
 - If K = ∅, take V = ∅.
 - Otherwise choose ρ > 0 with C := {x : dist(x, K) ≤ ρ} ⊆ G (K compact, G open). C is compact and C ⊆ U, so μ(C) < ∞ by (R1).

subproblems.title: Support of a current from a mass–measure identity
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n, and μ a measure on ℝ^P such that M_W(T) = T.massOn W = μ(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P. Then spt T = T.support = U ∩ spt μ. Here spt μ = μ.support (x ∈ spt μ iff μ(N) > 0 for every neighbourhood N of x), and spt T = U ∖ zeroRegion(T), where zeroRegion(T) is the union of all open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and T(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = μ W) → T.support = U ∩ μ.support

Source: steps 6 and 7 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 2.11 and Remark 3.2(3)), with the mass identity of part (a) taken as the hypothesis.

Notation.
- |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2}, the sum over strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P, with e_I = (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}).
- 𝒜_W = {ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) : tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x}, and M_W(T) = T.massOn W = sup{ofReal T(ω) : ω ∈ 𝒜_W} in [0, ∞].

 - From the formula, |cα| = (Σ_I c²·α(e_I)²)^{1/2} = |c|·|α| for c ∈ ℝ.

subproblems.title: Representing measures of the same current coincide
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n, and R₁, R₂ ∈ IMRep U n two integer multiplicity representations of T (R₁.Represents T and R₂.Represents T). Then R₁.measure = R₂.measure, i.e. θ₁·H^n⌞M₁ = θ₂·H^n⌞M₂ as measures on ℝ^P.
